mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's shots-for being below Team B's shots-against average AND (b) Team A's shots-on-target-for relative to Team A's shots-for (conversion rate proxy). Measure whether the ratio of shots_on_target-for to shots-for for Team A, crossed with Team B's shots_on_target-against rate, predicts Team A goals-for beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals-for rises with the joint product of Team A's shots-on-target-for rate and Team B's shots-on-target-against rate, even when Team A's raw shot volume is below Team B's; the relationship saturates as shot volume increases beyond a threshold.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume deficit relative to Team B is jointly associated with a conversion-efficiency gap: when Team A produces fewer shots but Team B allows a higher shots-on-target rate against them, the joint relationship between Team A's shots-for, Team A's shots-on-target-for, and Team B's shots-on-target-against determines whether Team A's goal output is suppressed or sustained relative to its shot count.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) for two sides simultaneously — not a single observable against one opponent-descriptor band. The conversion-rate proxy (shots_on_target / shots) is a non-linear ratio, and the cross-team conditioning on both Team A's offensive efficiency and Team B's defensive leakage cannot be reduced to any single-observable mirror or coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: measure Team A goals-for H1 vs H2 crossed with Team B goals-against H1 vs H2. The joint half-level asymmetry (Team A back-loaded scoring, Team B's H1 vs H2 defensive profile) is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals in this fixture rise relative to first-half goals when Team A's historical back-loading of goals-for aligns with Team B's half-level defensive vulnerability pattern; the combined second-half goal rate exceeds the first-half rate more than the competition baseline would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal production relative to first-half goal production is jointly conditioned on Team B's asymmetric half-level goal-conceding pattern: Team B concedes more in the first half (0.793 against in H1) than the second half (0.902 against in H2 — actually slightly more in H2), while Team A scores more in the second half (0.789 FOR H2 vs 0.422 FOR H1). The joint half-level scoring and conceding profiles of both teams together determine whether total goals are front- or back-loaded.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses a within-match state split (half-level) for both teams simultaneously — a two-dimensional half-level conditioning across two sides. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it requires the joint half-level profiles of Team A's offensive timing and Team B's defensive timing to be measured together.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's fouls-for being above competition average AND (b) Team B's fouls-for being above competition average. Within that joint condition, measure whether the combined foul load predicts cards_2h above the level predicted by either team's card rate alone. Team A fouls-for (11.876) and Team B fouls-for (12.315) both exceed competition average (11.753); Team A yellow-cards-for (2.233) exceeds competition average (2.009).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards rise with the joint above-average foul production of both teams; the relationship is non-additive — the combined foul surplus predicts cards_2h more than the sum of individual team card rates would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate and yellow-card rate jointly interact with Team B's foul rate to determine second-half card volume: when both teams have above-competition-average foul rates, the second-half cards (cards_2h) are elevated beyond what either team's card rate alone predicts, reflecting a compounding disciplinary dynamic.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across three distinct observables (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) for both teams simultaneously, with a non-linear (compounding/interaction) structure. It cannot be reduced to a single observable against one opponent-descriptor band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A's recent possession (RECENT_5: 41%) being substantially below its all-prior average (47.7%) and below Team B's away possession (48.7%). Within this low-possession regime, measure whether Team A's corner-kicks-for rate (all-prior: 4.213, recent-5: 3.4) declines proportionally, sub-proportionally, or supra-proportionally relative to the possession drop — testing for a threshold or saturation in the possession-to-corners relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner-kicks-for rate declines as possession falls below a threshold, but the relationship is non-linear: corner production does not decline proportionally with possession loss, suggesting a saturation or floor effect at low possession levels.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession deficit (recent 5-match average of 41% vs Team B's 46.8% away) jointly interacts with Team A's corner-kick generation to determine whether low-possession teams can sustain corner volume: when Team A's possession drops significantly below 50%, its corner-kicks-for rate may diverge from what possession alone would predict, revealing a non-linear relationship between possession level and corner production.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a threshold/non-linear dependence of one observable (corners) on a continuous level of another observable (possession), not a simple coarse band. The joint use of two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) with a non-linear conditioning structure is not reducible to a single-observable mirror or one-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's H1 vs H2 corners-for split AND Team B's H1 vs H2 corners-against split. Both profiles show a consistent back-loading pattern. Measure whether the joint alignment of both teams' half-level corner profiles predicts a larger H2-vs-H1 corner differential than the competition baseline or either team's profile alone would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corners in the second half exceed total corners in the first half by a margin greater than the competition baseline when both the attacking team's H2 corner-production tendency and the defending team's H2 corner-conceding tendency are jointly elevated above their respective H1 levels.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's half-level corner production (H1: 1.771 FOR, H2: 2.446 FOR) and Team B's half-level corner conceding (H1: 2.274 AGAINST, H2: 2.857 AGAINST) jointly determines whether corner volume is back-loaded in this fixture: both teams' half-level corner profiles point in the same direction (more corners in H2), and the joint alignment of these two distinct half-level profiles — one offensive, one defensive — is the mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level splits for two distinct roles (Team A offensive, Team B defensive) simultaneously — a two-dimensional half-level conditioning. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it requires the joint half-level profiles of both teams to be measured together, and the alignment of both profiles is the structural feature being tested.
